### 1. User expression and simulator behaviour
- Target object: the customer's Home Comfort Financing account that paid for the March 2025 Performance Series installation ("pay off whatever is left on the financing today, in full, and have the account closed as paid off").
- Timing: today. Action boundary: a full payoff paid by herself, "by bank transfer rather than a card", from her new checking account; "not after a quote for later and you are not disputing anything".
- Authorisation: the simulator states it will accept "whatever the agent says needs to be put on the account or sorted out on their side first" ("that is fine and to go ahead"), will accept a figure only "stated to the cent", and will execute a handed-over payoff once "for exactly the amount and account the agent gave you". It never volunteers steps. Identity: phone 6145555417 + address 5127 Hayden Run Rd (email / PIN if asked).
- The simulator is passive: conveys the need, answers if/else, runs the user-owned payoff tool when handed over.

### 2. Act now / wait / refuse
- Act now. `find_finance_accounts` returns account 43b9bedd-… on the "18-Month 0% APR Equal Payment Plan", status `active`, `funded_date` 2025-03-14, `promo_end_date` 2026-09-13, `monthly_payment` 600.48, `payment_due_day` 13, `autopay_enrolled` False, `account_balance` 341.84.
- Visible grounds: full_payoff_payments — "A borrower who pays the account off in full pays the payoff figure, and that payment closes the account as paid off on the day it is made." payoff_quotes_and_closure §3 — paid off when balance reaches 0.00. repayment_terms_by_plan — "Penalty for paying early: none". The payoff is a user-owned tool ("This is the customer's own tool. The agent unlocks … and hands it over").
- But the payoff figure is not yet fixed (see item 6), so two agent-side postings must land first; neither is a reason to wait or refuse, since both can be posted today (posting day for each is "the first day after that period's statement closes" = 2026-10-01 = today).

### 4. Scored parameters
Date of handling / day of payoff = 2026-10-01. Account age = whole months 2025-03-14 → 2026-10-01 = 18.

**(a) Late fee, statement period 2026-09** (late_fee_posting_reference: charged "for every statement period whose required payment is still unpaid more than the plan's late-fee grace period (in calendar days) after its due date"; grace 10 days per schedule_of_charges; due 2026-09-13 = day 0; only 250.00 paid on 2026-09-10; still unpaid on day 11 = 2026-09-24 and on 2026-10-01).
- Computation document (late_fee_amount_and_ceiling): scheduled late fee × (100 − late-fee relief %) / 100, capped at the late-fee ceiling % (100) × monthly payment, rounded half up once.
- Scheduled late fee (late_fee_step_schedule, read with late_fee_lookback_window): most recent late-fee reversal posted 2025-12-04 → 9 whole months before 2026-10-01 (< 12), so the lookback "covers late fees posted less than as many whole months … as have passed since the most recent late fee reversal" = < 9 whole months. The only late fee (posted 2025-12-01) is 10 whole months old → outside. Count 0 → $25.00. (Records that led me there: the `late_fee` and `late_fee_reversal` lines of the transaction history.)
- Late-fee reliefs (added together, applied once):
  - account age (account_age_late_fee_relief): 18 months → 10 percent (funded_date on the account).
  - member (member_late_fee_relief): Comfort Club Gold active, 9 consecutive terms → 20 percent (Comfort Club agreement record).
  - payment record (payment_record_late_fee_relief): payments posted < 12 whole months before 2026-10-01 = autopay 2025-10-13 … 2026-08-13 (11) + debit card 2025-12-04 + online 2026-09-10 = 13; returned-payment entries in the span = 1 (2025-11-17) → count 12 → 10 percent.
  - total 40 percent.
- Fee = 25.00 × 60 / 100 = 15.00; ceiling 600.48 not reached → **15.00**.

**(b) Post-promotional interest, statement period 2026-09** (post_promotional_interest_charges; posted on 2026-10-01 after the late fee).
- Computation document (post_promotional_interest_calculation): base × rate × accrual days / 100 / 365, rounded half up once. Accrual days: no interest charge yet → from the day after the promotional end date (2026-09-14) up to but not including 2026-10-01 → 17 days.
- Base (post_promotional_interest_base): most recent payment (2026-09-10) not returned; a late fee (the 15.00 posted 2026-10-01) is in the last month → base = balance 356.84 − 15.00 = 341.84.
- Rate: post-promotional APR 17.99 (plan_rate_sheet) reduced once by post-promotional reliefs:
  - member (member_post_promotional_relief): 15 percent;
  - account age (account_age_post_promotional_relief): 18 months → 5 percent;
  - leftover (leftover_balance_post_promotional_relief): payments posted total 11069.89 less returned 600.48 = 10469.41 stood; leftover 10800.00 − 10469.41 = 330.59; / 600.48 = 0.5505 → at most 1 → 20 percent;
  - payment record (payment_record_post_promotional_relief): count 12 → 10 percent;
  - total 50 percent → rate 8.995.
- Charge = 341.84 × 8.995 × 17 / 36500 = 1.43212… → **1.43**.

**(c) Payoff figure** (payoff_figure + factors), after (a) and (b): balance 358.27.
- Payoff principal = balance less late fees, returned-payment fees and interest posted < 1 whole month before payoff = 358.27 − 15.00 − 1.43 = 341.84.
- Per-diem days (payoff_per_diem_day_count, rows read top-down): a payment has posted and the most recent interest charge (2026-10-01) posted later than the most recent payment (2026-09-10) → from 2026-10-01 through 2026-10-01 = 1 day.
- Starting rate (payoff_per_diem_starting_rate): promotion ended before the day of payoff → post-promotional APR 17.99.
- Payoff reliefs: member 15 (member_payoff_relief); account age 5 (account_age_payoff_relief, 18 months); leftover 20 (leftover_balance_payoff_relief, promotion ended, measure 0.5505); payment record 10 (payment_record_payoff_relief, promotion ended, count 12) → 50 percent → 8.995.
- Per-diem interest = 341.84 × 8.995 × 1 / 36500 = 0.08424…; payoff = 358.27 + 0.08424… = 358.3542… → **358.35**.
- Payment method `online_ach` ("pays once from a checking or savings account by routing and account number"; customer: "bank transfer from my checking, not a card"); not `autopay_ach` (autopay is off), not `phone_payment` (the customer runs the tool herself).

**Fall-back numbers (computation documents only, no factor):**
- Late fee: plan late fee 39.00 × 100/100, ceiling 600.48 → 39.00 (≠ 15.00).
- Post-promotional interest: base = balance on posting day 380.84 × 17.99 × 17 / 36500 = 3.19 (≠ 1.43).
- Payoff: per-diem rate = "The plan's APR" = 0.00 % on this plan (plan_rate_sheet contract APR) → payoff = balance 384.03 (≠ 358.35). With no prerequisites at all, the naive payoff is the current balance 341.84.
- Every product figure the computation documents name (plan late fee, ceiling %, grace period, plan APR, post-promotional APR) is stated in schedule_of_charges / plan_rate_sheet under the same names; the fall-backs are definite.

**Factor findability** — each factor document was reached from the words the records use: the `late_fee` / `late_fee_reversal` lines → "late fee", "late-fee reversal" (lookback, step schedule); `funded_date` → "account age … funded"; the Comfort Club agreement record (`Comfort Club Gold`, `active`, `consecutive_terms`) → the member relief documents, which name "Comfort Club Maintenance Agreements" and "consecutive terms"; `payment` / `payment_returned` lines → payment-record and leftover reliefs; `promo_end_date` → post-promotional starting rate and day count. ### 6. Problem tree derived from the visible materials
Problems: P0 = full payoff (customer's own write); P1 = late fee for 2026-09; P2 = post-promotional interest charge for 2026-09.
Edges: P0 ← P1; P0 ← P2; P2 ← P1. Order: P1 → P2 → P0.

- **Hop P0 ← P1 (state-derived).** full_payoff_payments: "The payoff figure is fixed only after the account carries the late fee owed for every statement period whose installment stayed unpaid past its grace period." Records: 2026-09 installment due 09-13, only 250.00 posted 09-10, no `late_fee` line with statement_period 2026-09; today is past day 10. The write that brings the state about was found by the sentence's own words "late fee … statement period … unpaid … grace period": late_fee_posting_reference ("A late fee is charged … for every statement period whose required payment is still unpaid more than the plan's late-fee grace period … posted on the first day after that period's statement closes") and its agent tool. (2025-11 already carries a late-fee line.)
- **Hop P0 ← P2 (state-derived).** full_payoff_payments: "The payoff figure is not fixed until the account carries the post-promotional interest charge for every statement period that closed after the promotion ended." Records: promo_end_date 2026-09-13; the 2026-09 statement closed 2026-09-30; no `interest` line exists. Write found via "post-promotional interest charge … statement period": post_promotional_interest_charges ("posted once for each statement period as an interest charge on the first day after that period's statement closes").
- **Hop P2 ← P1 (state-derived).** post_promotional_interest_charges: "The post-promotional interest charge for a statement period is worked out only after the account carries the late fee owed for that same period whenever its installment stayed unpaid past its grace period". Same records as hop 1 → the 2026-09 late fee must be on first.
- No hop was pre-solved: no document names another problem's tool, a route or an aggregated chain; each prerequisite sentence sits in the blocked problem's own document and names a record-visible state.

### Two-way counter-proof
- "Do only the payoff (quote 341.84, or balance + per-diem at 0 %)" is excluded by the two prerequisite sentences of full_payoff_payments read against the records (missing 2026-09 late fee and 2026-09 interest line). A payoff of 341.84 would also leave the figure "not fixed" under the visible rule.
- Posting interest before the late fee is excluded by post_promotional_interest_charges' prerequisite sentence (and would change the base row of post_promotional_interest_base).
- Late fee for 2025-11 again: excluded by L3 (period already carries a late fee line). No late fee for 2026-10 (period not closed / not past grace).
- Lookback alternative (12 whole months, giving one earlier fee → $32.00): excluded by late_fee_lookback_window "The reversal test is read first".
- Payoff day-count alternative "day after promotional end date" (18 days): excluded because row 1 ("most recent interest charge posted on a later day than the most recent payment") is read first and holds once P2 is posted.
- Payoff per-diem rate alternative "plan's APR 0.00": excluded by payoff_per_diem_starting_rate row 1 (promotion ended → post-promotional APR).
- Payment-record count boundary: autopay 2025-09-13 is exactly 12 whole months before → excluded ("less than 12 whole months").
- Payment method: `online_ach` per the method definitions and the customer's stated method.
- Observation (to be carried to dependency_form): payoff_per_diem_day_count worked case 1 uses "Most recent payment 10 September; most recent interest charge 1 October" (hypothetical, day of payoff 14 October) — dates coincide with this task's post-write records; payoff_figure's worked example uses "Day of payoff 1 October". Both are labelled hypothetical and do not state this customer's tier.
